raw: | A `mxcli test` case whose body does `retrieve … where [id = '[%CurrentUser%]']` fails with only **FAIL:exception during execution** — nothing says what was raised | Two things at once. Runtime: tests run in `Core.createSystemContext()` (`endpoint.go`), a system session with no user, so the `[%CurrentUser%]` token cannot resolve and the retrieve throws; `[id = $currentUser]` only *seems* to work because `$currentUser` is empty there and matches nothing. mxcli: `rewriteBodyForVerdict` wrapped every CALL in an `ON ERROR` handler that set a **fixed** verdict text and discarded the error | `cmd/mxcli/testrunner/generator_endpoint.go` (`rewriteBodyForVerdict`), `.claude/skills/mendix/test-microflows/SKILL.md` | Concatenate the error: `'FAIL:exception during execution: ' + $latestError/Message`. No new measurement needed — `throwsHandler` already uses the same expression, measured at 0 errors on mxbuild 11.6.0 and 11.13.0. A generic catch-all verdict is the same defect class as a decorative assertion: it hides the one fact that diagnoses the failure. The skill now says plainly that tests have no current user and that user-scoped logic is tested by passing the user/account as a parameter. Not changed: the legacy after-startup runner's log-line `Exception during execution` (its runtime log already carries the stack trace). ChipCoV9 #5 |
